chapter_theme: The soul as purusha and as anu (அணு, the atom): the Lord made speech, bonds and the tattvas from beginningless time; he is the atom within the atom and is in the soul as the soul is in him; the tiny soul, like a banyan seed, can be cleared of the dark of bonds and set on the good path.

2007.reading: Speech beginning with vaikhari, the impurities beginning with maya, the distinctions beginning with purusha that bear false witness, and the particular workings of knowledge and action that bear true witness: the Lord who acts made all these from beginningless time.
2007.nuance: கரி (witness) closes three compounds, பொய்கரி, மெய்கரி, செய்கரி, a word game hard to fix. புருடாதி பேதம் are the tattvas from purusha down. The claim that the Lord made even the bonds 'without beginning' (அனாதியே) is central to Siddhanta, as tradition reads it.

2008.reading: The first Lord is the atom within the atom; for those able to approach the atom within the atom, by dividing that atom of atoms into a thousand parts, approaching the atom within the atom becomes possible.
2008.nuance: அணு is both 'atom' and, in Siddhanta, the soul (anu), so 'the atom within the atom' may be the Lord within the soul. The verse repeats அணுவில் அணுவினை in every line; the thousand parts mark extreme subtlety.

2009.reading: If one makes the soul pure by the light, as with the seed of the spreading banyan, driving out the painful darkness of bonds, one can seek the good path that leads on.
2009.nuance: The banyan seed is tiny but holds a great tree, a traditional image for the soul's hidden capacity. சுடர் (the light) is unnamed; it is commonly taken as grace or knowledge. நடர்கொண்ட is obscure.

2010.reading: People do not perceive the seamless mingling in which he is in the soul and the soul is in him; the peerless Lord, being everywhere, stood without lessening as all that moves and does not move.
2010.nuance: கணு அற (without joint or seam) stresses that the mingling has no join; the verse holds both indwelling (he in the soul) and containment (the soul in him).

links.note: Both measure subtlety by repeated division: 2008 divides the atom into a thousand to reach the Lord in it, 2011 divides a cow's hair into a hundred and then a thousand to give the soul's size.

source_issues: 2009 line 4: நடர்கொண்ட is obscure; it may be a corruption of நடைகொண்ட.
